screen-recording.context: A monitor with a ring and record dot on its screen. Used for screen capture tools, tutorials, demos and recording a desktop or app window.

flip-camera.context: A camera body with two curved arrows circling its lens. Used to switch between the front and rear camera on phones and video calls.

virtual-background.context: A person in front of a framed scene with a mountain and sun. Used for video call settings that replace or blur the real room behind you.

hybrid-meeting.context: A wall screen showing two faces above two people seated at a table. Used for meetings where some people are in the room and others join by video.

video-bar.context: A slim camera bar with a central lens sitting on top of a monitor. Used for conference room cameras and all in one video call hardware.

watch-party.context: Two viewers under a screen that shows a play triangle. Used for shared viewing features where friends stream a video together in sync.

camcorder.context: A handheld video camera with a front lens barrel, a viewfinder and a small side screen. Used for home video, filming and retro camera themes.

broadcast-camera.context: A studio television camera with a lens hood and viewfinder on a wheeled pedestal. Used for live TV, studio production and broadcasting topics.

film-cartridge.context: A small film canister with a spool knob on top and a tongue of film. Used for analog photography, 35mm film and film stock.

video-timeline.context: Two tracks of clip blocks with a vertical playhead line. Used for video editors, cutting clips and arranging footage in sequence.

screenplay.context: A stack of script pages with two round fasteners on the left edge and short lines of text. Used for film and TV scripts and screenwriting tools.

color-grading.context: Three colour wheels each with a small marker dot off centre. Used for video colour correction tools and colour grading panels.

cue-card.context: A large card with bold lines of text held up by a hand. Used for prompts in television, speeches and acting, where lines are shown off camera.

video-switcher.context: A production panel with a grid of square buttons and a fader lever. Used for live video mixing, switching camera feeds and streaming control rooms.

field-monitor.context: A small monitor with a folding hood flaring around the screen and a stand. Used for on set previews, camera operators and outdoor viewing.

film-projector.context: A vintage movie projector with two reels on top and a lens at the front. Used for cinema, old movies and screening rooms.

magic-lantern.context: An old lantern shaped projector with a chimney on top and a lens tube at the front. Used for history of projection, slides and Victorian entertainment.

box-office.context: A ticket booth with an awning, a service window and a small speaking hole. Used for cinemas, theatres, events and buying tickets in person.

video-cassette-recorder.context: A low box with a wide tape slot and a clock display on the front. Used for retro video, VHS recording and old home entertainment.

microfiche.context: A card with a cut corner, a header strip and a grid of tiny frames. Used for library archives, old records and microform reading.

tv-guide.context: A schedule grid with a time bar on top and rows of programme blocks. Used for TV listings, channel guides and what is on now.

slow-motion.context: A play triangle followed by a shortening trail of lines and a dot. Used for slow playback, replay speed controls and slow motion video.

360-video.context: A play triangle inside an elliptical ring with an arrowhead. Used for panorama and surround video, VR clips and 360 degree cameras.

hd-video.context: A rounded rectangle containing the letters H and D. Used for high definition video quality settings and labels.

4k-resolution.context: A rounded rectangle containing the characters 4 and K. Used for ultra high definition video and display quality labels.

test-card.context: A screen with two vertical bars and a circle at the centre. Used for TV test patterns, calibration and no signal screens.

static-noise.context: A television with rabbit ear antennas and a screen covered in scattered dots. Used for no signal, interference and glitch themes.

news-desk.context: A newsreader behind a curved desk with a screen on the wall behind them. Used for TV news, anchors and newsroom features.

voice-over.context: A microphone next to a video frame with a play triangle. Used for narration, dubbing and recording a voice track over video.

transcript.context: A document with lines of text, each starting with a small speaker marker. Used for speech to text output, interview transcripts and captions.

ham-radio.context: A radio transceiver with a tuning knob, a display, an antenna and a hand microphone on a cord. Used for amateur radio and two way radio.

radio-tuner-dial.context: A tuning window with tick marks and a pointer rising above it. Used for radio tuning, frequency selection and analogue receivers.

signal-booster.context: A small box with two upright antennas and signal arcs between them. Used for range extenders, repeaters and improving phone or wifi coverage.

cell-tower.context: A tall lattice mast with panel antennas near the top. Used for mobile networks, coverage and telecom infrastructure.

mobile-hotspot.context: A smartphone sending wifi arcs upward from its top edge. Used for tethering and sharing a phone internet connection.

airplane-mode.context: An airplane silhouette inside a rounded square. Used for the setting that switches off all wireless radios during flights.

submarine-cable.context: A round cable cross section with a ring of strands around a central core. Used for undersea internet links and cable construction.

telephone-pole.context: A utility pole with a crossarm, two insulators and wires drooping to each side. Used for power lines, phone lines and overhead cabling.

microwave-relay-tower.context: A lattice tower with two bowl dish antennas facing opposite ways. Used for point to point radio links and telecom backhaul.

satellite-uplink.context: A ground dish aimed upward with a dotted beam reaching a small satellite. Used for satellite communication, ground stations and sending signals to space.

signal-interference.context: Three signal bars beside a jagged zigzag line cutting through. Used for weak signal, jamming and noisy connection warnings.

telegraph-key.context: A Morse key with a flat base, a pivoting lever and a round finger knob. Used for Morse code, telegraphy and early wireless.

ticker-tape-machine.context: A glass dome on a small stand with a paper tape curling out. Used for historic stock prices and old telegraph printers.

teletype.context: A boxy teleprinter with a paper sheet feeding out the top and a keyboard at the front. Used for telex, old terminals and early text communication.

speaking-tube.context: A curved voice pipe with a small cap at one end and a flared bell mouth at the other. Used for ship bridges, old buildings and pre electric intercoms.

signal-fire.context: A flame rising above crossed logs. Used for beacons, warning fires and old long distance signalling.

heliograph.context: A round mirror on a tripod with a sighting rod beside it. Used for sun flash signalling, survey history and old military communication.

signal-lamp.context: A round lamp with horizontal shutter slats across its lens and a carrying handle. Used for ship to ship light signals and Morse by lamp.

semaphore-telegraph.context: A tall post with a crossbeam and two movable arms at the top. Used for optical telegraph towers and history of long distance messaging.

alarm-bell.context: A flared bell with a clapper below and short ring marks at its sides. Used for alerts, fire bells and warnings that something is ringing.

fire-alarm-pull.context: A wall box with a flame symbol above a pull handle bar. Used for fire alarm stations and emergency evacuation points.

buzzer-button.context: A square buzzer unit with a large round push pad and a cable trailing away. Used for quiz games, game shows and answer buttons.

cipher-disk.context: Two concentric rings divided into cells around a centre pin. Used for secret codes, cryptography and puzzle games.

app-badge-count.context: A rounded app tile with a small circular badge at its top right corner. Used for unread counts and notification numbers on app icons.

ringtone.context: A smartphone with a music note beside it. Used for choosing call sounds and notification tones.

digital-signage.context: A tall vertical screen on a floor stand showing a picture block and a line of text. Used for advertising displays, menu boards and information kiosks.

press-camera.context: A vintage press camera with a viewfinder on top, a large lens and a round flash reflector at the side. Used for photojournalism and old news photography.

press-hat.context: A brimmed hat with a small card tucked into its band. Used for old time reporters, journalism and press themes.

rolled-newspaper.context: A newspaper rolled into a tube with two bands around it and a spiral end. Used for paper delivery and the daily news.

digital-newspaper.context: A tablet showing a newspaper page with a headline bar, columns and a picture block. Used for news apps and online editions.

breaking-news.context: A television banner with a lightning bolt at its left end and lines of text. Used for urgent news alerts and live headlines.

news-ticker.context: A long strip with scrolling text blocks and a small arrow at its right end. Used for scrolling headlines and news crawls.

interview-microphone.context: A handheld reporter microphone with a square station cube around its neck. Used for street interviews and TV reporting.

reporter-notebook.context: A tall narrow spiral pad bound at the top with lines of notes. Used for journalists, shorthand and quick note taking.

classified-ads.context: A newspaper page divided into many small boxed ad blocks in columns. Used for small ads, listings and notices.

zine.context: A small stapled booklet with a star on its cover. Used for handmade magazines, self publishing and small press.

tear-off-flyer.context: A sheet with a pin at the top and a row of vertical tear off tabs along the bottom. Used for community notice boards and lost and found posters.

protest-sign.context: A rectangular placard with lines of bold text on a stick. Used for rallies, marches and demonstrations.

skywriting.context: A small plane trailing a looping smoke line. Used for aerial messages, stunt flying and airshows.

aerial-banner.context: A small plane towing a long wavy banner on a line. Used for beach advertising and aerial promotions.

blog-post.context: A browser window with a heading bar and text lines, with a pen nib over the corner. Used for writing and publishing web articles.
